## Changes since v2.3.5

- Added the authenticated V2 protocol over a TLS connection, including local enrollment, per-install client credentials, and client revocation.
- Added opt-in remote access on selected network interfaces with short-lived, one-time pairing files.
- Kept legacy V1 lighting disabled by default and loopback-only when enabled; legacy process-management commands remain unavailable.
- Legacy client device filters now apply to that client's handshake without reconfiguring shared devices. New server configurations enable all nine providers; existing provider lists remain unchanged.
- Existing server-wide filters from old versions can be reviewed and optionally reset from the tray, without silently discarding the owner's choices.
- Added stable device identities and V2 device discovery, lighting, request, and lease handling.
- Added concurrent authenticated clients and per-client lighting priority controls in the server tray. At equal priority, the first authenticated client retains precedence across reconnects during the server run.
- Added authenticated shutdown requests. A request stops the server only when no other authenticated session remains and legacy V1 access is disabled; an auto-started server allows a short grace period for concurrent V2 clients to disconnect. Legacy V1 has no reliable disconnect signal, so the server stays running while legacy access is enabled. Auto-starting MineLights clients verify the server's launch identity before requesting shutdown on exit.
- Added MineLights Server and client version 2.4.0.
